questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The government is developing a new test __in the recruitment and training of teachers__ in the upcoming session.

options.text: in recruitment and training on teachers
of the recruitment and training of teachers
for the recruitment and training of teachers
for recruitment or training of teachers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. for the recruitment and training of teachers .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition **"for"** is the most appropriate choice when expressing the purpose or intention of an action, which is applicable in this context.
 
• The phrase **"for the recruitment and training of teachers"** clearly conveys the purpose of the test being developed by the government.
 
• Other prepositions like **"in"**, **"of"**, or **"on"** do not convey the intended meaning as accurately as "for."

Correct sentence: *The government is developing a new test for the recruitment and training of teachers in the upcoming session*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**
 
 
• **For:** Indicates purpose or intention. Example: This is a tool for cutting wood.
 
• **In:** Indicates inclusion or location. Example: She is in the room.
 
• **Of:** Indicates possession or relation. Example: The tail of the dog is wagging.
 
• **On:** Indicates position or surface. Example: The book is on the table.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.

The fleets of Anthony were __not merely defeated, also destroyed__ by Augustus Caesar.

options.text: not only defeated, but also destroyed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. not only defeated, but also destroyed .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses the phrase “not merely defeated, also destroyed.” This is grammatically incorrect and does not convey the intended meaning effectively.
 
• The phrase "not only... but also" is the correct correlative conjunction pair that expresses both actions (defeated and destroyed) effectively.
 
• By choosing **option 1**, the sentence becomes grammatically correct and clear in meaning.

Correct sentence: *The fleets of Anthony were not only defeated, but also destroyed by Augustus Caesar*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Use of Correlative Conjunctions:**
 
 
• **Not only... but also:** Used to join two related ideas, emphasizing both parts equally.
 
• **Example:** She is not only intelligent, but also hardworking.
 
• It ensures proper parallelism in sentence structure.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors to Avoid:**
 
 
• Incorrect pairing of correlative conjunctions, such as "not merely... also." This disrupts the flow and correctness of the sentence.
 
• Ensure that the phrases following "not only" and "but also" are grammatically similar for proper parallelism.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select "No substitution required".

The car, with all __its features, were meticulously__ designed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. its features, was meticulously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence, **"The car"**, is singular and therefore requires a singular verb.
 
• The verb **"was"** is correct as it agrees with the singular subject **"The car"**.
 
• The original sentence incorrectly used **"were"**, which is a plural verb and does not align with the singular subject.

Correct sentence: *The car, with all its features, **was meticulously** designed.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**

 
 
• Singular subjects require singular verbs, and plural subjects require plural verbs.
 
• Example of singular subject and verb: *The book **is** interesting.*
 
• Example of plural subject and verb: *The books **are** interesting.*
 
 
 
• **Compound Subjects:**
 
 
• If a compound subject is joined by **"and"**, it usually takes a plural verb.
 
• If a compound subject is joined by **"with," "along with," "together with,"** etc., the verb agrees with the main subject.
 
• Example: *The car, along with its passengers, **was** safe.*

• **"Obstacle"** is the most appropriate synonym for "hurdle," as it also refers to something that blocks or hinders progress. (अवरोध)
 
 
• **Example:** The team's unity helped them overcome every obstacle on their way to success.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Obstacle**.

• **Example:** Her family’s constant support encouraged her to pursue her dreams.
 
 
 
• **Encouragement** (प्रोत्साहन): Words or actions that provide confidence or motivation to someone.
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher’s encouragement boosted the student’s confidence before the exam.
 
 
 
• **Stimulus** (उत्तेजना): Something that provokes or causes a reaction, often in a positive way.
 
 
• **Example:** The announcement of rewards acted as a stimulus for the team to work harder.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

When they left for Mexico, their house was in __good__ condition than it is now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. better .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence compares the condition of the house in two different time periods — when they left for Mexico and its current state.
 
• In such comparisons, the correct word to use is the comparative form of "good," which is **"better."**
 
• Using other options like "more good," "excellent," or "best" is grammatically incorrect or contextually inappropriate in this case.

Correct sentence: *When they left for Mexico, their house was in **better** condition than it is now*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative adjectives:**

 
 
• Used to compare two things, e.g., "better," "worse," "taller," etc.
 
• Formed by adding "-er" to short adjectives or by using "more" with longer adjectives.
 
• **Example:** This book is **better** than that one.
 
 
 
• **Superlative adjectives:**

 
 
• Used to show the highest degree of comparison among three or more things, e.g., "best," "worst," "tallest," etc.
 
• Formed by adding "-est" to short adjectives or by using "most" with longer adjectives.
 
• **Example:** This is the **best** book in the library.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She received / an award / for her work / in a engineering field.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. in a engineering field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence has been divided into four segments: 
 
 
• **She received**
 
• **an award**
 
• **for her work**
 
• **in a engineering field**
 
 
 
• Segment 2, **"in a engineering field"**, contains a grammatical error.
 
• The article **"a"** is incorrect because it precedes the word **"engineering,"** which begins with a vowel sound. The correct article in this context is **"an."**
 
• The correct phrase should be **"in an engineering field."**

Correct sentence: *She received an award for her work in an engineering field.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Articles:**
 
 
• **"A":** Used before words that begin with a consonant sound. Example: *a book, a car*.
 
• **"An":** Used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Example: *an apple, an engineer*.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using the wrong article before a noun can make the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
• It is important to focus on the **sound** of the word that follows the article, not just the spelling.
 
 
</ul
